criteria.criterion: PrHost (or GhClient) gains a call that reads the repository's default branch via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` (`default_branch` field); Athena::land_pr uses it as NewPr.base and no longer uses git current_branch for the base.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. `PrHost::default_branch` is added, and `GhClient` implements it with `self.api("GET", "repos/{repository}")`, reading `default_branch` and failing if the field is empty or missing. `publish()` passes its result as `NewPr.base`. The `current_branch()` call is removed from `Athena::land_pr` (gh.rs lines 401-421 and 479-482).

criteria.criterion: A detached HEAD or a local branch absent from the remote no longer affects the PR base or errors.
criteria.evidence: Read the code. `Athena::land_pr` no longer reads the local branch at all; the base comes only from `host.default_branch()`. The work commit is built from the HEAD commit id, which also works on a detached HEAD.

criteria.criterion: The commit pushed to athena/<job> contains the candidate's content plus the job's records (verification, outcome, candidate and other records) from the local history, and is a descendant of the verified candidate so the push guard and fingerprint check still hold.
criteria.evidence: Read the code. `Git::commit_with_records` builds a tree from the candidate with `records/` replaced by the `records/` of local HEAD, then commits it with the candidate as its only parent. `publish()` runs the push guard on that commit and pushes it. Tests in athena-git and gh.rs assert the commit descends from the candidate, contains the records files, and has the same fingerprint as the candidate.

criteria.criterion: The merge call remains reachable only when `merge_via_rest` is true and checks are green; that gate and its default (off) are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Read the code. The gate `if job.merge_via_rest && seen == Checks::Green` is unchanged and is the only call to `host.merge`. The config default is not touched. The existing merge-gate tests still pass.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`: a new test using fake Runner/PrHost shows the base is the host-reported default branch (e.g. `trunk`) while the local branch differs; a new test shows the pushed commit includes the records files, not just the candidate commit.
criteria.evidence: 11 passed, 0 failed, including the three new tests: `the_client_reads_the_default_branch_from_the_repository`, `the_pull_request_targets_the_host_default_branch_and_the_work_commit` (base == "trunk"; the push, link head and checks all use the work commit) and `the_work_commit_carries_the_records_on_top_of_the_candidate` (the tree includes `records/jobs/bootstrap/{outcome,verification}.json`).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` , `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass; existing land_pr tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported ok with 0 failed. Clippy and fmt --check printed nothing and exited successfully.

findings.summary: Running land --pr again after a partial failure will probably be refused by the push guard.
findings.evidence: `publish()` builds a new work commit with `commit-tree` on every run. Outside tests (`Git::isolated` fixes the committer date) the commit gets the current timestamp. If a run pushes `athena/<job>` and then `open_pr` fails, the next run makes a commit with a different id. The remote head is then not an ancestor of it, so `check_push` refuses. Before this change the pushed commit was always the same candidate, so a rerun worked. Possible fixes: reuse the remote head when its tree matches, or make the commit deterministic. This is inferred from reading the code; I did not run it.

findings.summary: The work branch carries every record on local HEAD, not only this job's.
findings.evidence: All of `records/` is taken from local HEAD. This matches the criterion's wording ('and other records') and lets the PR merge cleanly onto main, but the PR diff may include records from unrelated jobs.

findings.summary: `land.rs` and `pr.rs` were listed as deliverables but were not changed.
findings.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, gh.rs, athena-git lib.rs and the design doc. The fix did not need those two files, and this fits the 'small' default.

summary: I recommend accepting this change. It fixes both bugs in `athena land --pr`. First, the pull request's base is now the default branch GitHub reports, read with `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` (field `default_branch`). The local current branch is no longer used, so a detached HEAD or a branch that isn't on the remote has no effect. Second, the pushed `athena/<job>` branch is now the verified candidate plus one commit on top. That commit replaces `records/` with the `records/` from local HEAD (verification, outcome and the rest), so merging the PR lands what `athena check --history` expects. The fingerprint stays the candidate's, and the stored link and the checks lookup both use the pushed commit. The `merge_via_rest` gate and its default (off) are unchanged. New tests cover the client call, the base being `trunk` while the local branch differs, and the records commit (its file list, ancestry and an equal fingerprint). I ran `cargo test -p athena-core gh` (11 passed), the full `cargo test` (all passed), `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` (both clean). There is one minor issue: if a run pushes the branch but fails before the PR is opened, running again will probably be refused by the push guard. Two other points are not defects: `land.rs` and `pr.rs` were listed as deliverables but needed no change, and the work branch carries every record on local HEAD, not only this job's.
